notes: Fresh write for this request; I re-checked every figure from the earlier interrupted attempt against the snapshot and code. Revenue growth for years 2-5 is 15/10/7/5% on code NTM revenue of about $492B. FCF margins are 42/44/44/43/42%, measured as CFO minus capex over revenue. History: FY2024 44.4%, FY2025 46.6%, FY2026 44.8%, TTM 41.9%, and H1 FY2027 39.4%, which is held down by a receivables build of -24.6B from extended payment terms and an inventory build of -10.2B. dcf_weight is 0.7. Offline check with the code's valuation.value() on the current generator inputs (code's compute is authoritative): terminal value is about 71.7% of EV, under 80%. DCF value is about $140 per share and the peer-relative value about $287 per share, blending to about $184. Against the $209.66 close on 2026-08-26 that is about -12% upside, which code rates Underperform. I did not tune inputs toward any target. UNRESOLVED, material, route to gen-mapping or the lead: code's net cash is -10.923B because short_term_investments is unmapped. It leaves out marketable debt securities of $34.143B ($33.003B US Treasury plus $1.140B agency, effectively cash) and marketable equity securities of $42.783B ($36.9B of NVDA's publicly held equity investments are under lock-up restrictions); both come from the periodic.txt balance sheet, and no XBRL concept in the snapshot carries them. Effect is about +$1.41 per share (debt securities only) to +$3.17 per share (both lines). On its own this would not move the price-to-target gap out of the Underperform band. For the writer and critics: H1 FY2027 net income includes $23.707B of net gains from equity securities (10-Q cash flow statement), so TTM P/E and EPS overstate operating earnings; the FCF here is CFO-based and excludes those gains.
